text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"Clear opening claim about driverless cars not being a necessity and being a safety threat","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a defensible position early and lets the reader know the essay's main line of argument."},{"evidence":"Explains that the cars are “not completely driverless” and must still rely on a human driver","quality":"use of source evidence","description":"It supports claims with specific information from the article rather than speaking only in generalities."},{"evidence":"Moves from general claim to examples of sensors, then to a counterargument, then back to conclusion","quality":"organization","description":"It has a more recognizable argumentative structure with a body that develops and revisits the position."},{"evidence":"“However, some people might argue...” followed by rebuttal","quality":"counterargument handling","description":"It acknowledges an opposing view and responds to it instead of ignoring it."},{"evidence":"Conclusion restates that driverless cars are not a necessity and are more of a technology development tool","quality":"conclusion effectiveness","description":"It ends by returning to the central claim and tying the discussion together."},{"evidence":"Uses transitions like “However,” “For example,” and “As of right now”","quality":"coherence","description":"Its ideas are linked more smoothly, making the argument easier to follow."}]}
